questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Whether making streets car-free is a good idea
How to cross busy roads safely with young children
Why buses in London are so slow during rush hour
The best shopping streets in the UK for tourists
questions.why: Rob says the show is about street safety and 'whether pedestrianisation is a good thing or not'.

questions.q: What benefits of pedestrianisation does Rob mention at first?
options: Cheaper shops, more jobs and more visitors to town
Faster buses and trains into the city centre
More parking spaces and wider roads for cars
No traffic, less noise and pollution, more safety
questions.why: Rob mentions no traffic, less noise and air pollution, and no chance of being knocked down.

questions.q: Why does the Mayor of London want to pedestrianise Oxford Street?
options: To attract more tourists
To deal with air pollution there
To build more shops
To make buses faster
questions.why: Rob says the Mayor wants to tackle air pollution in this very busy spot.

questions.q: What problem with banning traffic does Rob point out?
options: Shops lose customers
Pedestrians walk too slowly
The traffic just moves to other streets
It costs the city too much money
questions.why: Rob says the traffic doesn't disappear; it gets rerouted somewhere else.

questions.q: According to Joe Urvin, how has the number of cars in the UK changed?
options: It has fallen slowly since 1970 as people use trains
It has stayed at about 20 million since the 1970s
It rose from 20 million in 1970 to over 30 million
It has doubled from 20 million to 40 million
questions.why: He says there were 20 million cars in 1970 and now there are over 30 million.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the three problems Joe Urvin describes?
options: Not enough space on the streets
Pollution
People not walking enough
Too much noise at night
questions.why: His three problems are space and congestion, pollution, and people not getting enough exercise.

questions.q: Why are 'smart cities' looking at pedestrianisation, according to Joe Urvin?
options: To make cities more attractive and help local business
To reduce the number of tourists in the old town centres
To save money on road repairs and street lights
To stop people driving to work and parking in the centre
questions.why: He says it makes cities better and more attractive and helps build the local economy.

questions.q: What is Rob's opinion about banning all traffic from town centres?
options: It should happen in every city in the UK as soon as possible
He isn't sure, as it could make getting around hard
It is the only way to stop pollution in big cities
It would make no difference to the number of cars
questions.why: Rob says he's not sure, as banning all motorised traffic might make it hard for people to get around.
